alt.en: A printed book page numbered 102. Below the end of another carol and a short rule, the heading "God rest you merry, gentlemen." is followed by two verses, the first beginning "God rest you merry, gentlemen, Let nothing you dismay" and the second "In Bethlehem in Jury".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el número 102. Bajo el final de otro villancico y una raya corta, el título "God rest you merry, gentlemen." va seguido de dos estrofas: la primera empieza "God rest you merry, gentlemen, Let nothing you dismay" y la segunda "In Bethlehem in Jury".

caption.en: The carol on page 102 of William Sandys's Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London, 1833), among the carols he found still in use in the West of England, with the comma after "merry".
caption.es: El villancico en la página 102 de Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern de William Sandys (Londres, 1833), entre los villancicos que él encontró todavía en uso en el oeste de Inglaterra, con la coma después de "merry".

source: William Sandys, Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London: Richard Beckley, 1833), Part the Second, p. 102, "God rest you merry, Gentlemen"
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1833; William Sandys 1792-1874 (Internet Archive record). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed book page numbered 753, headed "Traditional tunes of uncertain date." Three paragraphs of text are followed by "God rest you, merry gentlemen" set as a tune with piano accompaniment, marked "Moderate time", in one sharp and common time, with the words under the notes.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el número 753 y el encabezado "Traditional tunes of uncertain date." Tras tres párrafos de texto viene "God rest you, merry gentlemen" como melodía con acompañamiento de piano, con la indicación "Moderate time", con un sostenido en la clave y en compasillo, y la letra bajo las notas.

caption.en: William Chappell's Popular Music of the Olden Time (London, 1855 to 1859), page 753: noting that the carol "is sometimes sung in a major key, and sometimes in a minor", he prints the minor tune we sing, in a copy noted down by Edward Rimbault.
caption.es: Popular Music of the Olden Time de William Chappell (Londres, 1855 a 1859), página 753: tras anotar que el villancico "is sometimes sung in a major key, and sometimes in a minor", a veces se canta en tono mayor y a veces en menor, imprime la melodía menor que cantamos, en una copia que anotó Edward Rimbault.

source: William Chappell, Popular Music of the Olden Time, vol. 2 (London: Cramer, Beale & Chappell, [1855 to 1859]), p. 753, "God rest you, merry gentlemen"
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1855 to 1859; William Chappell 1809-1888, G. A. Macfarren 1813-1887, Edward F. Rimbault 1816-1876. Faithful scan of a flat page; IA marks the record NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Robarts Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "1." and "God rest you, merry Gentlemen." in italics, with four-part harmony on pairs of staves in E minor, the words under the upper staff, a section marked "Chorus" on "O tidings of comfort and joy", and the page number 2 at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "1." y "God rest you, merry Gentlemen." en cursiva, con armonía a cuatro voces en pares de pentagramas en Mi menor, la letra bajo el pentagrama superior, una sección marcada "Chorus" en "O tidings of comfort and joy" y el número de página 2 al pie.

caption.en: No. 1 in Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old (London, first published 1867; this printing of the 1870s): John Stainer's four parts in E minor, the setting our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: El n.º 1 de Christmas Carols New and Old de Bramley y Stainer (Londres, publicado por primera vez en 1867; esta impresión es de la década de 1870): las cuatro voces de John Stainer en Mi menor, de las que parte nuestro arreglo.

source: H. R. Bramley and John Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old, first series (London: Novello, Ewer and Co., undated, [187?]), No. 1, p. 2, "God rest you, merry Gentlemen"
